assertions.text: The document makes no claim about Ruth's values or personality that would fit most teachers equally well (for example that she cares about students or wants to make a difference) unless the claim is tied to specific evidence from her material.
assertions.evidence: No generic "cares about students" claims. Every character claim is anchored: "You run on obligation to identifiable people" follows the finished/abandoned lists; "This is not a discipline problem. A discipline problem does not produce a four-year unbroken publishing streak."

assertions.text: Each claim the document makes about Ruth's strengths or working patterns names its evidence: a specific project, role, number, or quoted piece of feedback from her material.
assertions.evidence: Claims carry sources: "A commissioning editor... wrote: 'Your explanatory writing is genuinely strong, clearer than most of what crosses my desk.'"; "Two acceptances from eleven cold pitches is an 18% hit rate"; "1,924 copies at £9.99 with no marketing whatsoever, earning £6,290"; "never missed an issue in four years" (1,150 subs, 52%).

assertions.text: The document names a pattern that distinguishes Ruth's abandoned efforts (the YouTube channel, the tutoring-agency website, the twice-deferred MSc application) from the efforts she finished.
assertions.evidence: "a list of things somebody was waiting for, and things nobody was waiting for... Every completed thing had a named person or a fixed external obligation attached. Every abandoned thing required you to go out and manufacture demand from people who had not asked for you." — each of the three abandoned items is named.

assertions.text: The document uses her Teachers' Pension figures (the £14,800 a year already accrued, or the roughly £908 a year that each further year of service adds) when weighing any path that involves leaving employed teaching.
assertions.evidence: "if you walked out of Ashworth this afternoon and never taught again — you would have, at 68: Teachers' Pension: £14,800 a year ... Total: about £26,770" vs outgoings £19,440; and per-year accrual costs used to weigh exit: "Out of the scheme entirely | £1,598" (Paths 4/5).

assertions.text: The document states what full-time freelance science writing typically pays and compares that against the income Ruth's outgoings require.
assertions.evidence: No typical-pay figure for full-time freelance science writing appears. The nearest is qualitative — "most of our freelancers... don't make a living from features alone" — and the only comparison is to tutoring, not outgoings: "earn less than you currently make from tutoring three hours a week."

assertions.text: Ruth's actual submission record (11 pitches, 2 acceptances, £220 earned) is used as evidence when the document assesses her prospects as a writer.
assertions.evidence: "Your pitch record is not actually bad. Two acceptances from eleven cold pitches is an 18% hit rate." And Path 5: "the market has said no nine times out of eleven"; earnings framed as "less than you currently make from tutoring three hours a week" (£220 not restated).

assertions.text: Each proposed path is given its own distinct way of failing, different from the failure modes of the other paths.
assertions.evidence: P1: "If the voice goes properly at 54... you get ill-health retirement terms". P4: "removes the floor underneath the portfolio at exactly the moment you'd be finding out whether the portfolio works". P5: "the day-to-day work is the exact thing you have abandoned three times". P3 fails via "APE application is unsuccessful"/"Tutoring won't scale". P2 ruled out at her request, not modelled.

assertions.text: Every proposed path states an observable sign, within a stated time window, that would show the path is not working.
assertions.evidence: Only Path 3 gets falsifiers ("If it isn't drafted by summer 2027"). Paths 1, 4, 5 get verdicts with no sign or window: Path 1 "the richest path, and I don't believe it's available to you"; Path 5 "Verdict: **no.**" — nothing observable, no window.

assertions.text: At least one option is explicitly ruled out, deferred, or restructured because her £8,412 of savings cover only about three months of outgoings.
assertions.evidence: Savings appear only as a data inconsistency: "you have £8,412 saved and describe it as three months. I've used your stated figures throughout but treated the true surplus as uncertain." Paths 4 and 5 are rejected on pension/cash cost and push-channel fit, never on runway.

assertions.text: No recommended step requires Ruth to leave the Sheffield area before Alice finishes school in summer 2029.
assertions.evidence: Assumption 7: "**Sheffield is permanent.** ... I read that as permanent. No path here involves moving, and every non-teaching income line is remote or local by design." Calendar keeps her at Ashworth (0.8 in 2027, 0.6 in 2029); APE role is "approximately 20 days ... most of it remote."

assertions.text: The document commits to one recommended direction for Ruth, with its reasoning stated, rather than presenting the paths as equally weighted choices for her to pick from.
assertions.evidence: "## The answer first — **Reduce the classroom, don't leave it...**"; Path 3 "*(recommended)* ... **this is the one.**"; Path 5 "**no.**"; a "Why Path 3, in one place" section with six numbered reasons and a stated price of "£129,000 of net income and £13,900 a year of pension."

assertions.text: The document names the conflict between Ruth's statement that she is not a leader and the evidence of her leading in her record (running staff training, leading an exam-marking team of 11, mentoring early-career teachers), rather than silently accepting either side.
assertions.evidence: The Head of Science section accepts her side and defuses rather than names the conflict: "you're right that you'd hate it… Three independent people are telling you the same thing, and it is not 'you should be a manager.'" No mention that she already leads (team of 11, INSET, ECTs) contradicts "I am not a leader"; Marcus's "You lead in this school whether you admit it or not" is never engaged.

assertions.text: The recommended path's first steps are specific enough to begin within a few weeks: a named request, application, message, or task, not an instruction to explore, reflect, or network.
assertions.evidence: "August–September 2026 (do these now) — Apply for Assistant Principal Examiner. Closes 26 September 2026." Plus "Request your Teachers' Pension benefit statement and your Remediable Service Statement" and "Track spending for three months against money.csv." Named application, named request, dated.

assertions.text: The document names external events (in her school, the exam system, her finances, or Alice's plans) that should cause the plan to be re-examined.
assertions.evidence: "What would make me change my mind... Any of these should reopen the plan: **The APE application is unsuccessful**... **Tutoring won't scale past about six hours a week**... **An agent takes the trade book on with a real advance**... **Alice's plans change** — staying local, or needing more support than budgeted."
